### `GET /api/projects/{project_id}/synthetic/backends`

**List Synth Backends**

List the synth backends registered on this BrewSLM install +
each one's reachability (USER-SUCCESS Epic 5 Phase 5a).

``project_id`` isn't read — backends are install-global — but the
route lives under the project-scoped prefix to keep the URL
pattern consistent with the rest of the synthetic router (and to
keep the auth middleware applied uniformly).

Frontend uses this to decide whether to render the backend picker
on the playbook panel: if only one backend is available, the
picker is hidden to avoid clutter.

### `POST /api/projects/{project_id}/synthetic/generate-async`

**Generate Qa Async**

Kick off a batched QA-pair generation job. Returns immediately
with a ``task_id``; clients poll ``GET /synthetic/tasks/{task_id}``
for progress + accumulated pairs.

Lifts the 50-pair cap that the sync ``/generate`` endpoint enforces:
the server batches into ``PER_BATCH_ROW_CAP`` chunks and (when
``use_all_chunks`` is set) samples fresh source text per batch.

Hardening Phase H2 — also spawns a shadow Job mirroring progress
into the top-bar notification bell.

| `api_url` | `string` | no |  |

### `GET /api/projects/{project_id}/synthetic/playbooks`

**List Synth Playbooks**

Catalog of registered playbooks compatible with the project's
selected recipe.

When the project has no recipe selected (legacy projects pre-dating
the auto-apply-on-create fix), this returns an empty list plus
``recipe_required=True`` so the UI can render a "pick a recipe
first" prompt instead of a confusing dump of every playbook
across every task shape — none of which would actually run, since
``run_playbook`` requires ``selected_recipe`` to dispatch.
Brief-driven + magic-create projects always have a recipe applied
at creation time (see ``recipe_service.default_recipe_for_*``)
so this branch is now legacy-only.

### `POST /api/projects/{project_id}/synthetic/check-plan-rules`

**Check Plan Rules**

Check the pending structured-plan rows against a caller-supplied plan-rules document (deterministic, no model).
``dry_run`` (default ``true``) answers with counts per rule and sample row ids and changes nothing. With
``dry_run=false`` every pending row that breaks a ``reject``-severity rule is marked rejected as
``rule_violation:<rule id>``; they stay on disk (grouped by rule in the review queue's Rejected section), can be
restored, and are never purged. ``?async_job=true`` runs it as a ``plan_rules_check`` Job. A bad rules document is a
`400` with ``error_code: invalid_plan_rules`` and the pointer of the problem.

Body: ``rules`` (the document as an object, or its JSON text), ``dry_run``, optional ``row_ids``, ``source``,
``synth_job_id``, ``max_rows``.

The same document can be passed as ``params.plan_rules`` to the structured-plan ``scenario_grid`` playbook: after schema
validation, a plan breaking a ``reject`` rule is dropped as ``rule_violation`` (the Job's reject summary lists the rule
ids) and ``warn`` rules only annotate the accepted row (``plan_rule_warnings``).

A rules document (up to 64 KB, 200 rules):

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "rules": [
    {"id": "widget-size-cap", "type": "step_requires", "severity": "reject",
     "description": "a created widget stays small",
     "match": {"tool": "invoke_operation", "operation": "create_widget"},
     "require": {"path": "args.arguments.body.size", "op": "max", "value": 10}},
    {"id": "gadget-binds-sturdy-widget", "type": "ref_requires",
     "match": {"operation": "bind_gadget"},
     "ref": {"path": "args.arguments.body.widget"},
     "creator": {"match": {"operation": "create_widget"}, "name_path": "args.arguments.body.name"},
     "require": {"path": "args.arguments.body.kind", "op": "equals", "value": "sturdy"},
     "on_missing": "violate"},
    {"id": "verify-after-create", "type": "requires_step", "severity": "warn",
     "if": {"operation": "create_widget"}, "then": {"tool": "verify"}},
    {"id": "no-create-and-retire", "type": "forbid_together",
     "a": {"operation": "create_widget"}, "b": {"operation": "retire_widget"}}
  ]
}
```

Rule types: ``step_requires`` (every step matching ``match`` must satisfy ``require``), ``ref_requires`` (each value a
matching step holds at ``ref.path`` names an object created by a step matching ``creator.match`` whose ``creator.name_path``
equals it; that creating step must satisfy ``require``, ``before: true`` also demands it come earlier, and a reference no
step creates is a violation unless ``on_missing`` is ``ignore``), ``requires_step`` (if a step matches ``if`` some step must
match ``then``), ``forbid_together`` (steps matching both ``a`` and ``b`` must not coexist; ``same_step`` narrows to one
step). A match is ``{tool, operation, operation_regex, where}``; a condition is ``{path, op, value, quantifier}`` (ops
``equals not_equals in not_in exists not_exists regex contains max min``) or ``all`` / ``any`` / ``not`` of conditions.
Semantics worth knowing: every op except ``not_exists`` FAILS when its path resolves to nothing (``exists`` / ``not_exists``
only look at presence); a leaf condition's ``missing: "pass"`` makes a value op pass instead (default ``"fail"``). Steps are
ordered by LIST POSITION (the model's ``step`` number is used only in messages, so duplicate or shuffled numbers cannot
fool ``before``). A list-valued ``ref.path`` contributes each item as a reference. With ``before: true`` and several creators,
a reference violates only when NO creator precedes it, and ``require`` is checked on the preceding creators; without
``before``, every creator must satisfy ``require``. A rule may carry its own ``steps_path`` (e.g. a verification list).
Regexes: patterns are capped at 200 characters, nested-quantifier patterns such as ``(a+)+`` are refused, and a regex only
sees the first 10,000 characters of a value; the check itself runs in a worker thread.

Optional top-level ``paths`` (``tool`` default ``tool``, ``operation`` default ``args.operation``) and ``steps_path`` (default
``steps``).

### `POST /api/projects/{project_id}/synthetic/review-queue/restore`

**Restore Rejected Synth Rows**

Undo a soft-reject: rejected rows matching the selectors go back to ``pending`` with their reject reason (and
``plan_rule_ids``) cleared. Selectors: ``reject_reason`` (exact; ``""`` = rows rejected without one),
``reject_reason_prefix`` (e.g. ``rule_violation:``), ``row_ids`` (at most 5000); at least one is required and all given
must match (`400` ``invalid_restore_request`` otherwise). ``dry_run`` (default ``true``) returns ``matched`` and
``by_reason`` counts; ``dry_run=false`` restores them.

### `POST /api/projects/{project_id}/synthetic/review-assist`

**Review Assist**

Pre-screen pending synthetic rows with an LLM: each gets a verdict (pass / fail / unsure),
a reason code and a one-sentence note, shown in the review queue (filter / group by them,
then bulk accept or reject). Runs as the ``synth_review_assist`` Job (``?async_job=true``;
a dry run answers inline). Verdicts live in a sidecar, never in ``synthetic.jsonl``.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project_id` | `path` | `integer` | yes |  |
| `async_job` | `query` | `boolean` | no |  |

**Request body** (required)

Content type: `application/json` — `ReviewAssistRequest`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `backend` | `string \| null` | no | Any synth backend pin (ollama:&lt;model&gt;, command:&lt;model&gt;, cloud:&lt;provider&gt;:&lt;model&gt;, ...); omitted = the first reachable local backend. |
| `use_batch` | `boolean` | no | Anthropic Message Batch (half price; cloud:anthropic:&lt;model&gt; only). |
| `row_ids` | `integer[] \| null` | no | Pending row ids to judge (default: every pending row). |
| `source` | `string \| null` | no | Only pending rows of this synth_source group. |
| `synth_job_id` | `integer \| null` | no | Only pending rows written by this Job. |
| `rubric_text` | `string \| null` | no | Free text appended to the built-in rubric (e.g. the allowed operations). |
| `rows_per_call` | `integer` | no |  |
| `max_rows` | `integer \| null` | no |  |
| `dry_run` | `boolean` | no | Report how many rows / calls the run would take; call no model. |
| `only_missing_judge` | `boolean` | no | Skip rows this judge (the backend) already has a valid verdict for (resume). |
| `consensus` | `string[] \| null` | no | Only rows whose current judge consensus is one of none / single / agree_pass / agree_fail / disagree. |
| `prior_verdicts` | `string[] \| null` | no | Only rows where another judge's valid verdict is one of pass / fail / unsure (e.g. a second opinion where the first said fail or unsure). |

**Responses**

| Status | Schema | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | `any` | Successful Response |
| `422` | `HTTPValidationError` | Validation Error |


### `GET /api/projects/{project_id}/synthetic/review-queue`

**List Synth Review Queue**

List pending synthetic rows for the project, grouped by
`synth_source` (USER-SUCCESS Epic 2b) — or by class label with
`?group_by=class` (Epic E), by originating failure cluster
(`cluster`), by the Job that wrote the rows (`job`) or by the backend
that wrote them (`backend`), by review-assist verdict (`verdict`) or by
verdict + reason code (`assist_reason`) or by judge consensus (`assist_consensus`).
`?synth_job_id=` / `?synth_backend=` / `?verdict=` / `?reason_code=` / `?assist_consensus=` / `?judge=`
narrow every list (`judge` shows one judge's verdicts; verdict / reason then read that judge).

Pending rows are gated out of dataset prep — they don't enter
training until the user accepts them via `/review-queue/bulk-update`
(or rejects them, in which case they're deleted).

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project_id` | `path` | `integer` | yes |  |
| `group_by` | `query` | `string` | no |  |
| `synth_job_id` | `query` | `integer` | no |  |
| `synth_backend` | `query` | `string` | no |  |
| `verdict` | `query` | `string` | no |  |
| `reason_code` | `query` | `string` | no |  |
| `assist_consensus` | `query` | `string` | no |  |
| `judge` | `query` | `string` | no |  |

**Responses**

|---|---|---|

### `POST /api/projects/{project_id}/synthetic/run-playbook`

**Run Synth Playbook**

Run a playbook against the project's gold rows, generate
synthetic training data, and persist accepted rows into the
project's synthetic dataset.

Returns a PlaybookResult: rows + backend_used + elapsed_sec +
prompt_snippet.

Hardening Phase H1 — pass ``?async_job=true`` to enqueue the
playbook as a background Job. The endpoint returns 202 +
``{job_id: ...}`` immediately and the user tracks progress in
the notification bell. The synchronous path is preserved for
backward compatibility and for short, low-volume runs where a
spinner is fine.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project_id` | `path` | `integer` | yes |  |
| `async_job` | `query` | `boolean` | no |  |

**Request body** (required)

Content type: `application/json` — `RunPlaybookRequest`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `string` | yes | Synth mode, e.g. 'positives_paraphrase'. |
| `target_count` | `integer` | no |  |
| `target_class` | `string \| null` | no |  |
| `backend` | `string \| null` | no | Optional backend pin, e.g. 'ollama:llama3.1:8b'. |
| `use_batch` | `boolean` | no | Anthropic Message Batches: the run's calls go as one batch per stage at half the list price; results take minutes to hours, unanswered calls are retried directly. `cloud:anthropic:<model>` backends with `?async_job=true` only (400 `invalid_playbook_param` otherwise). A run that fails or is cancelled after its batch still reports the batch spend on the Job. |

**Responses**

| Status | Schema | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | `any` | Successful Response |
| `422` | `HTTPValidationError` | Validation Error |

### `POST /api/projects/{project_id}/synthetic/review-queue/bulk-update`

**Bulk Update Synth Review Queue**

Bulk accept or reject pending synth rows. Accepted rows flip
to ``review_status="accepted"`` and become eligible for
training; rejected rows flip to ``review_status="rejected"``
(Arc 5 soft-reject) and stay on disk for review + bulk-purge.
Pass ``reject_reason`` to tag each rejected row with a label
the Rejected section's group-by-reason UI uses.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project_id` | `path` | `integer` | yes |  |

**Request body** (required)

Content type: `application/json` — `BulkReviewQueueRequest`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `row_ids` | `integer[]` | yes | IDs of pending synth rows to update. |
| `action` | `string` | yes | 'accept' or 'reject'. |
| `reject_reason` | `string \| null` | no | Optional label for a bulk reject (e.g. 'duplicate', 'schema_invalid'). Stamped on each rejected row so the Rejected section can group + purge by reason. |

**Responses**

| Status | Schema | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | `any` | Successful Response |
| `422` | `HTTPValidationError` | Validation Error |

Accept or reject *every pending row* in one ``synth_source`` group by

Studio review-queue panel's pending groups (Epic E — actionable workbench),

| `action` | `string` | yes | 'accept' or 'reject'. |
| `reject_reason` | `string \| null` | no | Optional label stamped on each rejected row (reject only). |

**Responses**

| Status | Schema | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | `any` | Successful Response |

### `POST /api/projects/{project_id}/synthetic/review-queue/recheck-code-format`

**Recheck Code Format Endpoint**

Re-check pending code examples labelled json / yaml / toml / xml: code that does not parse as its label
is a mislabel. ``dry_run`` (default) counts by language; otherwise those rows are marked rejected with
reason ``language_mismatch`` (reversible, never purged).

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project_id` | `path` | `integer` | yes |  |

**Request body** (optional)

Content type: `application/json` — `RecheckCodeFormatRequest`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

| `row_ids` | `integer[] \| null` | no | Apply only to these rows; each is re-validated (still pending and still a mismatch). Omitted = every mismatch. |

step. Pass ``reasons`` to purge a specific reason cohort
(e.g. just the ``duplicate`` rows); omit to purge every
rejected row.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reasons` | `string[] \| null` | no | When set, only rejected rows whose ``reject_reason`` is in this list get physically removed. When omitted (or empty), all rejected rows are purged. |

| Status | Schema | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | `any` | Successful Response |
| `422` | `HTTPValidationError` | Validation Error |

### `POST /api/projects/{project_id}/synthetic/run-playbook/dry-run`

**Dry Run Synth Playbook**

Pre-flight a playbook with target_count=1 against the chosen
model — **without persisting** any rows. The frontend calls this
before kicking the real async job so a refusal or empty-output
failure surfaces in &lt;10s inline on the panel, instead of after a
60-180s job that ends in a notification-bell error.

Returns the same envelope as ``/run-playbook`` plus:

  - ``accepted_count``: number of rows that passed validation.
  - ``refusal_detected``: True when the LLM returned a short
    non-JSON apology that ``_looks_like_refusal`` recognised.
  - ``raw_llm_snippet``: first ~280 chars of the model's response
    so the user can see exactly what came back.
  - ``ok``: convenience flag — True only when accepted_count &gt;= 1
    AND refusal_detected is False.

Never raises for refusals or 0-row outputs — those land as
``ok: False`` in a 200 response so the frontend can render an
inline error + retry-with-different-model affordance. 4xx is
reserved for genuine input errors (unknown mode, missing recipe,
missing gold set) and 5xx for backend transport failures.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project_id` | `path` | `integer` | yes |  |

**Request body** (required)

Content type: `application/json` — `RunPlaybookRequest`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `string` | yes | Synth mode, e.g. 'positives_paraphrase'. |
| `target_count` | `integer` | no |  |
| `target_class` | `string \| null` | no |  |
| `backend` | `string \| null` | no | Optional backend pin, e.g. 'ollama:llama3.1:8b'. |
| `use_batch` | `boolean` | no | Accepted and ignored: the dry run is always one direct call. |

**Responses**

| Status | Schema | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | `any` | Successful Response |
| `422` | `HTTPValidationError` | Validation Error |

### `GET /api/projects/{project_id}/synthetic/backends/cloud/models`

**List Cloud Models**

Curated cloud-LLM catalog (OpenAI / Anthropic / Deepseek) +
which providers have an API key saved for THIS project. Drives
the synth panel's cloud picker so the user sees:

  - all three providers + curated model lists
  - a green check + "Key saved" badge for providers with creds
  - a "Save key first" prompt for providers without creds

Project secrets live under ``cloud_llm_<provider>:api_key`` (the
same coordinates the gold-generate flow uses), so a user who's
already saved a key in one panel sees it pre-filled in the other.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project_id` | `path` | `integer` | yes |  |

**Responses**

| Status | Schema | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | `any` | Successful Response |
| `422` | `HTTPValidationError` | Validation Error |


### `GET /api/projects/{project_id}/synthetic/backends/ollama/models`

**List Ollama Models**

List the Ollama models installed on the local daemon, used by
the Synth panel's model-picker dropdown.

Returns ``{models: [...], default: <pattern-matched-model>}``.
The ``default`` reflects what the platform's auto-pick would
choose given current `PREFERRED_MODEL_PATTERNS` so the picker
can label it ``"Auto (qwen2.5:14b...)"``.

Best-effort — if Ollama isn't reachable, returns
``{models: [], ollama_available: false, error: ...}`` with a
200 so the picker can render a 'No Ollama models found' state
rather than failing the panel load.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project_id` | `path` | `integer` | yes |  |

**Responses**

| Status | Schema | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | `any` | Successful Response |
| `422` | `HTTPValidationError` | Validation Error |
